overview: This Senate resolution names September 2026 National Child Awareness Month, timed to the start of the school year. It aims to raise awareness of charities and youth organizations that help children and to recognize their work as important to the country's future. It specifically calls attention to children who have experienced homelessness, foster care, trafficking, violence or trauma, those with serious physical or mental health needs, and the value of arts programs and efforts to close learning gaps. It does not change any law or provide money. The Senate approved it on August 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say the month encourages people to support groups that help children, especially the most vulnerable, at a time of year when families and communities are already focused on kids.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, so it adds no new help for the children it highlights.
